description.html: This decorative mask resembles an old hockey mask from horror movies. The surface is yellow-green with darker green shading, covered in rows of small dimples, with a riveted strap on top and small riveted tabs on the sides. It looks as if it has lain underwater for a long time, so it fits nicely into an aquarium with green plants and a darker substrate.

The two large eye holes act as a passage that fish swim and play through. The mask is a good choice for aquariums with lively fish that like to explore, and children often find it their favorite detail in the tank. Combined with themed decorations such as skulls or shipwrecks, it creates a striking, slightly spooky setup.

Before placing the mask, rinse it with lukewarm water, without soap. It looks best upright, leaning against a stone or root, or with the bottom edge buried in gravel, so it cannot fall over when fish dig or when you clean the bottom. Turn the eye holes toward the front glass so you can see the fish swim through. Algae in the dimples is easiest to remove with a soft brush.
